clue.text: No men on this side stick

definitions.meaning: the female line of a family is called its ... side, the side with no men
the cleft stick that held wool or flax for hand spinning

explanation.surface: A rule that no men may sit on one side, then an order to stick to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning was once women's work, so the spinner's staff came to stand for the female branch of a family as well as naming the tool itself.

clue.text: Nasal sign of a cold? We'd go back to doctor before work

indicators.note: go back tells us the letters of we'd are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as its letters W, E, D
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold resolves to see a doctor before heading in to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns WED into DEW; DR and OP follow it, as 'before' places them. The question mark admits the definition is playful: a drip at the end of a cold nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet hanging from a runny nose is jokily likened to the bead of moisture on morning grass.

clue.text: Haunt this plot for mint?

definitions.meaning: a haunt is a place one visits often, a favourite spot
read as a patch of ground where a mint stamps out coins, rather than one where the herb grows

explanation.surface: A ghostly question about a garden bed where mint is grown.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite place someone frequents is idiomatically their usual patch; the second reading pictures the land where coins get struck.

clue.text: Grey-looking hay's tossed

indicators.note: hay that is tossed is thrown about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word with its S, as written

explanation.surface: Hay being tossed in a field has turned a dull grey.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe hides that the S of hay's is part of the fodder: 'tossed' rearranges all four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is pale grey, so something ash-coloured looks grey.

clue.text: Overheated, some prefer ventilation

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: People who are too hot would rather have the windows open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals that the answer sits inside 'prefer ventilation', spanning the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheated in the figurative sense of passionate or impassioned matches ardent zeal.

clue.text: Cult cut up, lacking place of torment

indicators.note: lacking means a part is missing, so those letters come out of the longer word

parts.note: to dissect is to cut up a body for study
Dis is the Roman underworld, and in Dante the lower city of hell

explanation.surface: A cult has been broken up, and now lacks a hell to threaten followers with.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is a classical name for hell or the underworld, a crossword regular; removing it from the front of DISSECT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is a small religious group with devoted followers, a splinter faction.

clue.text: Duck, embracing love, moped

indicators.note: one piece embracing another holds it inside, a container signal

parts.note: a scoter is a dark sea duck
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A duck hugs its beloved and then sulks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moped' looks like a verb meaning sulked, but it is the noun: a small motorised bike. 'embracing' puts O inside SCOTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorbike, much like a motor-driven two-wheeler for town use.

clue.text: Copper right? No, it is short

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the copper is right and is told it is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: CU, the chemical symbol, and RT are joined; 'No, it is' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt reply is brief to the point of rudeness, terse.

clue.text: Supplier of protective gear to opening pair

definitions.text: Supplier of protective gear to opening pair

parts.words: Supplier of protective gear to opening pair
parts.note: reads like a sports outfitter kitting out two cricket openers, but means the plant whose leaves covered Adam and Eve, the first couple, in Genesis

explanation.surface: A firm supplies pads and helmets to the two batsmen who open the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening pair suggests cricket's opening batsmen; it is Adam and Eve, the first humans, who covered themselves with leaves from this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first couple sewed its leaves together as their first garments.

clue.text: Action I call, sum being wrong. Find theerror

indicators.note: being wrong says these letters are not in their right order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checking a sum calls out that it is wrong and demands the mistake be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being wrong' rearranges the fourteen letters of ACTION I CALL SUM; 'Find' links to the definition, printed run together as 'theerror' (the error).
explanation.definitionFit: A miscalculation is a mistake in working something out, an arithmetical slip.

clue.text: Protection from the rain Borg- Wade employed

indicators.note: employed is read as put to use in a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the tennis names Borg and Wade, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Tennis players Björn Borg and Virginia Wade are used as cover from a shower at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' shuffles THE RAIN BORG WADE. Borg and Wade were Wimbledon champions, famous for rain delays.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping boards fixed to an outside wall shield a building against wind and wet.

clue.text: Carried away with wound, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: wound, as in wound round, means wrapped

explanation.surface: An injured person carried off on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind: wrapped, which is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enraptured or entranced is carried away by delight.

clue.text: Massive foot in country-dance

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other here

parts.note: a hey is a country dance with interweaving figures

explanation.surface: A huge foot stamping in a country dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A hey (or hay) is an old English country dance; FT goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hefty means heavy and bulky, much like weighty or large.

clue.text: Cliff shows sign of injury

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside, common in northern English place names
the mark left on the skin where a wound healed

explanation.surface: A cliff face bears the marks of damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated words: one a rocky crag in northern English dialect, the other a healed wound's mark.

clue.text: The Spanish in harbour stay on board

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bay is a sheltered stretch of water, a natural harbour
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards in port decide to remain on their ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On board here is nautical: to belay is to make a rope fast round a pin or cleat, and as an order it means stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors belay a rope by securing it, so the line holds firm and stops running.

clue.text: Allow extra leave free

definitions.meaning: to ... someone time is to allow them it
... as an adjective, surplus or additional
to ... a victim is to let them go unharmed

explanation.surface: An employer grants some additional time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to grant or afford, surplus to need, and to show mercy by not harming.

clue.text: Hanging makes little impression on writer

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the impression piece follows the writer piece

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
a dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: A hanged man leaves little mark on the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendent is the adjective meaning suspended, dangling.

clue.text: Peel's RU members, scrummaging, drive back

indicators.note: a rugby scrum is a struggling mass of bodies, so the letters are jostled about

explanation.surface: Members of Peel's rugby union team pack down in a scrum and push the other side back.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union; 'scrummaging' shuffles PEELSRU, and 'members' only completes the picture of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to beat it back, repel it.

clue.text: Hottest period? Take time in shadows

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely, to dog them
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Advice to take a break in the shade during the hottest spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shadows' looks like shade but is a verb: dogs. Put DAY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultry weeks of high summer were named after Sirius, the Dog Star, rising with the sun.

clue.text: Shortfall is handy around here in France

indicators.note: around means one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: deft means skilful with the hands
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A handy French location is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps DEFT round ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount by which money falls short.

clue.text: Wild threats knock the stuffing out of people

definitions.text: knock the stuffing out of people

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are let loose and run in any order

explanation.surface: Fierce intimidation leaves people deflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges THREATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter people is to devastate them emotionally, leave them crushed.

clue.text: Drinking bout in transport on the

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Drinking bout in transport on the', ends at 'the': CAR + OUSE needs a word for the river Ouse that is missing, and no scan or search supplies it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Drinking bout in transport on the

clue.text: Unconventional antique country

parts.note: a curio is a rare or quaint collectable object
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An odd old object from a far land.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean strange or odd, departing from the usual.

clue.text: May the president shortly turn out to have understanding of others' views

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: P is a short form of president

explanation.surface: Hope that the president will prove sympathetic to opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' shuffles MAY THE together with P.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the ability to share and grasp another person's feelings.

clue.text: Overwork fellow with diary

parts.note: a log is a daily record, a diary

explanation.surface: A man keeps a journal of his excessive working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog a horse or idea is to exhaust it by driving it too hard.

clue.text: Composer to evade awkward question

definitions.meaning: to fend off or sidestep a tricky query

explanation.surface: A composer dodges a journalist's tricky question.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Hubert Parry wrote the music for Jerusalem; and to deflect a blow or question is the fencing move.

clue.text: What size fuse needed for a seductress?

definitions.text: What size fuse needed for a seductress?

parts.words: What size fuse needed for a seductress?
parts.note: the rating of a household fuse in amps, with the Roman numeral for five in front, read as one word for a femme fatale

explanation.surface: An electrician asks what fuse a temptress requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuses are sold as 3, 5 or 13 amp; a 5-amp fuse written with the Roman V gives the word for a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her charm to seduce and exploit men.

clue.text: Jacob's wife in meadow next to hospital

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: The patriarch's wife lies in a field beside a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Laban's elder daughter was married to the patriarch before Rachel.

clue.text: Author's drink in japan

definitions.meaning: pen name of H. H. Munro, writer of short stories
a variant spelling of the Japanese rice wine sake

explanation.surface: A writer's drink while visiting Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Munro wrote under this pen name; the same letters spell a variant of rice wine from Japan.

clue.text: Ten into Slavonic dances-the traditional sort

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters move about and change places

explanation.surface: Ten people join a Slavonic folk dance, the traditional kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges all fifteen letters of TEN INTO SLAVONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to established customs and norms is a traditional type.

clue.text: Carbonize this fish

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken by burning
the Arctic ..., a fish related to trout and salmon

explanation.surface: An instruction to burn this fish to a crisp.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb for blackening by burning, and one coldwater trout-like fish.

clue.text: Scottish river engulfs pub in wood

indicators.note: one piece engulfs another by swallowing it whole, a container signal

parts.note: the Spey is a river in north-east Scotland famed for whisky distilleries
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A Scottish river floods a pub in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfs' puts INN inside SPEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small copse or thicket of trees.
